title: Uber Executive Overseeing Robotaxi Expansion to Depart
source_used: Transport Topics (Bloomberg page paywalled: bot check)
key_facts: Sarfraz Maredia, Uber's global head of autonomous mobility and delivery, will leave on 16 Nov 2026 after more than 12 years with the company.
He is leaving to pursue a top executive role at an undisclosed company outside transportation, according to an Uber spokesperson.
His duties will be split between Samarth Kejriwal, a senior director who oversees driverless-vehicle operations, and Aaron Emrich, who heads autonomous delivery.
Transport Topics calls it the latest of several departures in Uber's autonomous division this year, when key partnerships with Alphabet's Waymo and Serve Robotics unravelled.
Guy Peterson, head of business development for autonomous partnerships, joined Rivian spinoff Also as chief business officer this month.

Uber does not build its own cars; it partners with robotaxi makers and has more than a dozen partners, though most efforts have stayed limited in scale because they rely on yet-to-be-produced robotaxis or local regulations.
Maredia said Uber's focus remains scaling autonomous vehicles in more cities (per Transport Topics' summary).
quote_evidence: Sarfraz Maredia, who has been with the company for more than 12 years, is leaving to pursue a top executive role at an undisclosed company outside of the transportation industry, according to an Uber spokesperson.

Maredia's responsibilities will be split between Samarth Kejriwal, a senior director who currently oversees driverless vehicle operations and has been with Uber for more than a decade, and Aaron Emrich, who heads up autonomous delivery.
Uber's autonomous division has seen a number of executive departures in a year when key partnerships with Alphabet Inc.'s Waymo and Serve Robotics Inc. unraveled.
why_it_matters_hint: Another senior exit from Uber's robotaxi effort, in a year of partnership setbacks.
